item.title: Codex Skills: Folders, Install and Disable (2026)
item.description:
A Codex skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file. The file holds a name, a description and the steps for one job. Codex sees the name and description at the start, and reads the full steps only when a task matches. Put the skill in the right folder, and Codex finds it on its own or when you type $ and its name.

What is in a skill folder?

A skill is a folder. Only SKILL.md is required. The other parts are optional:

item.title: Claude Code MCP: Add, Scope and Remove Servers (2026)
item.description:
What is an MCP server in Claude Code?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets Claude Code use outside tools. An MCP server is a small program or remote service that offers tools, such as “search notes” or “save this fact”. Once you add a server, Claude can call its tools in any session that loads it. You set servers up with the claude mcp commands, not by editing settings by hand.

item.title: How to Install Claude Code (2026): macOS, Windows, Linux
item.description:
What is Claude Code?

Claude Code is Anthropic’s coding agent that runs in your terminal. It reads your project, edits files and runs commands. You install it once on your machine, then start it with claude in any project folder. Its memory comes from files such as CLAUDE.md and from optional add-ons.

How do you install Claude Code?

Open a terminal and run the command for your system. Anthropic’s native installer is the recommended route, and it keeps itself up to date.

item.title: How to Install Codex CLI (2026): macOS, Windows, Linux
item.description:
To install Codex CLI, run one command for your system. On macOS or Linux, run curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh. On Windows, use the PowerShell line below. Then run codex in a project folder and choose Sign in with ChatGPT. Codex CLI is OpenAI’s coding agent that runs in your terminal, on your own machine.

What is Codex CLI?

Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally. It reads the files in your project folder, edits them, and runs the tools already on your machine. It is separate from the Codex web agent at chatgpt.com/codex and from the Codex desktop app. The official README lists the IDE extension, the desktop app (codex app) and the cloud agent as other ways to use Codex.

item.title: How to Install Gemini CLI (2026): npm, Homebrew, GEMINI.md Memory
item.description:
To install Gemini CLI, run one npm command. Run npm install -g @google/gemini-cli, then run gemini in a project folder and sign in with Google. Gemini CLI is Google’s open-source coding agent for the terminal.

What is Gemini CLI?

Gemini CLI is a command-line coding agent from Google. It reads and edits files in your project folder, and it runs commands in your terminal. The official repository is github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli. Read 2026-11-12.

item.title: 如何安装 Claude Code（2026）：macOS、Windows、Linux
item.description:
什么是 Claude Code？

Claude Code 是 Anthropic 的编程 agent，在终端里运行。它读取你的项目、编辑文件并运行命令。你在电脑上安装一次，然后在任何项目文件夹里运行 claude 启动它。它的记忆来自 CLAUDE.md 等文件，以及可选的插件。

如何安装 Claude Code？

打开终端，运行适合你系统的命令。Anthropic 推荐的是原生安装器，它会自己保持最新。

系统 命令 更新方式
macOS、Linux、WSL curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash 自动，在后台进行
Windows PowerShell irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex 自动，在后台进行
Windows CMD curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.cmd -o install.cmd && install.cmd && del install.cmd 自动，在后台进行
Homebrew（macOS、Linux） brew install --cask claude-code 手动：brew upgrade claude-code
WinGet（Windows） winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode 手动：winget upgrade Anthropic.ClaudeCode
npm（任何装有 Node.js 22+ 的系统） npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code 手动：npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest

Anthropic 的安装文档还列出了 Debian、Ubuntu、Fedora、RHEL 和 Alpine 的 apt、dnf 和 apk 软件源。这些安装同样需要手动升级。npm 安装不要加 sudo。

item.title: Claude Code Hooks: Every Event and How to Use Them for Memory (2026)
item.description:
What are Claude Code hooks?

Claude Code hooks are commands that run at fixed points in a session. You set them in a JSON settings file, and Claude Code runs them when the event fires, with no model choice involved. They are the only part of Claude Code’s setup that runs code on its own, which makes them the main way to save or reload memory automatically.

The Claude Code hooks reference lists 33 events. The ones that matter most for memory are SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PreCompact and SessionEnd.

item.title: Claude Code Release Notes: Memory and Context Changes (2026)
item.description:
What are the Claude Code release notes for memory?

Claude Code’s memory is made of files (CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, rules) plus compaction, which shortens a long conversation when it nears the context limit. This page tracks the release notes that change how those parts behave. It covers the 11 newest GitHub releases, read on 2026-11-13, and skips releases that touch no memory or context behavior.

Memory-related changes by version

Version Date Change that matters for memory
2.1.323 2026-11-12 Fixed running /compact again, or after /context, summarizing away a message Claude had not answered yet. Fixed subagent transcripts and large tool results being saved apart from the session’s transcript after entering a worktree.
2.1.322 2026-11-10 Fast mode on Vertex. No memory change.
2.1.321 2026-11-09 Fixed new messages not saved, and claude -p and SDK sessions hanging, when memory ran out while the transcript was read. claude -p on Linux now exits 1 (not 0) when an NFS export loses transcript lines. Fixed auto mode losing a background subagent’s report when the conversation was compacted.
2.1.319 2026-11-06 /context no longer sends its full visual grid to Claude on every later turn. Its table keeps the 10 largest rows per list. /rename now warns when the name cannot be saved to the transcript.
2.1.318 2026-11-04 Fixed idle compaction replacing a conversation with a reply that was not a summary. Removed the fix that kept earlier thinking when resuming old conversations (that thinking can now be dropped).
2.1.317 2026-11-03 Fixed “Prompt is too long” after automatic compaction when a very large CLAUDE.md had changed since it was last sent. Fixed very long conversations losing their earlier summary when compaction had to shorten its own request.
2.1.316 2026-10-31 Fixed /model <id> not warning when the model is unknown. Auto-compact then assumes a 200K context window. Fixed the SDK not loading the CLAUDE.md of a directory outside the working folder.
2.1.314 2026-10-30 Added idle compaction to VS Code and the Claude Desktop Code tab: a conversation over 200K tokens that sits idle is summarized, and the summary is used on your next message if the prompt cache has expired. Each PreCompact hook’s output is now cut at 10,000 characters.
2.1.312 2026-10-27 Fixed Claude overwriting a very large CLAUDE.md, rules file or @-included file after reading only its start. Write now asks Claude to read the whole file or edit it in place.
2.1.311 2026-10-26 Fixed Claude seeing stale MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md content right after automatic compaction, when those files had been edited earlier in the session. Fixed freezes caused by a very long list item in CLAUDE.md.

Version 2.1.322 has no memory change. The GitHub list has no release numbered 2.1.313 or 2.1.315.

item.title: OpenClaw Skills (2026): Install from ClawHub, Write SKILL.md, Safety
item.description:
OpenClaw skills are folders of instructions that teach the agent a task, such as a calendar, a Todoist client or a database backup. You install them from ClawHub, the public registry, or write your own. A skill is not memory. It does not store what the agent learns. For that, see OpenClaw memory and the OpenClaw guide.

Sources: the OpenClaw ClawHub docs (documentation.openclaw.ai/clawhub) and the skill format page (documentation.openclaw.ai/clawhub/skill-format). Both read 2026-11-11.

item.title: OpenClaw Skills（2026）：从 ClawHub 安装、编写 SKILL.md、安全注意事项
item.description:
OpenClaw skills 是一些文件夹，里面放着教 agent 完成某项任务的指令，例如日历、Todoist 客户端或数据库备份。你可以从公共注册表 ClawHub 安装，也可以自己编写。skill 不是记忆：它不会保存 agent 学到的内容。关于记忆，请看 OpenClaw 记忆 和 OpenClaw 指南。

来源：OpenClaw ClawHub 文档（documentation.openclaw.ai/clawhub）和 skill 格式页面（documentation.openclaw.ai/clawhub/skill-format）。两者都在 2026-11-11 读取。

命令

你想做什么 命令 文档中的说明
查找 skill openclaw skills search "calendar" 在 ClawHub 中搜索
安装一个 openclaw skills install @openclaw/demo 记录来源，之后的更新仍然走 ClawHub
更新全部 openclaw skills update --all OpenClaw 原生命令
发布或删除 clawhub CLI（npm i -g clawhub） 需要先运行 clawhub login。用于发布、删除和恢复
安装插件（不是 skill） openclaw plugins install clawhub:<package> 插件和 skill 是两回事

文档说，原生 openclaw 命令会安装到当前 OpenClaw 工作区。单独的 clawhub CLI 会安装到你运行命令的文件夹下的 ./skills，并写入 .clawhub/lock.json。每个 skill 只用其中一种方式安装，这样你才知道它存在哪里。

item.title: OpenClaw 与 Hermes Agent 记忆对比（2026）：文件、上限、迁移
item.description:
OpenClaw 与 Hermes Agent 的记忆本质上是两种思路。Hermes 把记忆做得很小、很固定：两个有硬性上限的文件，以冻结快照的形式加载，外加对旧会话的全文搜索。OpenClaw 让记忆不设上限：Markdown 文件和每日笔记，支持混合搜索，并由后台任务把最好的笔记提升到 MEMORY.md。

两者都是开源（MIT）的 agent，都在你自己的电脑上运行，并通过聊天软件交互。Hermes 还有官方的桌面应用，与命令行共用同一套记忆。OpenClaw 来自 Peter Steinberger 和 OpenClaw Foundation；Hermes Agent 来自 Nous Research。下面的事实来自两个项目的文档，2026 年 10 月核对。

OpenClaw 和 Hermes 的记忆有什么不同？

两者都把记忆存成 agent 自己写的纯文本。Hermes 把记忆限制得很死，始终在上下文里约 1,300 个 token，其余内容都当作可搜索的历史。OpenClaw 让记忆以文件的形式增长，启动时只加载整理过的文件，其余内容通过语义和关键词搜索找回。

两者没有哪个“更好”。Hermes 的做法让提示词保持小巧，也让提示缓存保持稳定。OpenClaw 的做法能存更多内容，代价是需要 embedding 提供方和索引。两者都处在 AI agent 记忆入门 所讲的光谱的简单一端。

并排对比

Hermes Agent OpenClaw Hindsight（两者都可用的插件）
始终加载的文件 MEMORY.md（agent 笔记）、USER.md（用户资料） MEMORY.md（持久事实）、USER.md（可选资料） 无；记忆库在服务器上，按查询召回
位置 ~/.hermes/memories/ agent 工作区，默认 ~/.openclaw/workspace Hindsight Cloud、你自己的服务器，或本地嵌入式守护进程
大小上限 2,200 和 1,375 个字符，由工具强制执行 启动预算；超出则注入的副本被截断 没有固定上限；召回内容按你设的 max_tokens 预算裁剪
会话中途的更新 写入磁盘；提示在下次会话才更新（冻结快照） 文件写入磁盘；建立索引后搜索才能看到新笔记 retain 存入事实；之后的召回都能看到
每日或情景笔记 无；完整会话存在 SQLite 中 memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md 每日笔记 经历和世界事实，带时间和实体
搜索 session_search：对旧会话做 SQLite FTS5 全文搜索 memory_search：向量 + BM25 混合，带时间衰减、MMR 语义 + BM25 + 图 + 时间并行搜索，融合后重排序
需要 embedding 吗 不需要 可选（默认 OpenAI；可用本地 GGUF） 需要，由服务器处理
写入工具 memory 工具：添加、替换、删除 agent 写 Markdown 文件；memory_get 读取 retain：LLM 提取事实、时间、实体和关系
整理 记忆满了时 agent 必须先整理；后台复查 dreaming 任务把笔记提升到 MEMORY.md；压缩前先 flush 后台整理为观察和心智模型
写入审批 memory.write_approval: true 会暂存写入 dreaming 的输出进入 DREAMS.md 等待审阅 未列出
安全扫描 条目会扫描注入、外泄和不可见 Unicode 不可信的候选内容不会被提升 未列出
外部提供方 同一时间只能用一个：Honcho、OpenViking、Mem0、Hindsight、Holographic、RetainDB、ByteRover、Supermemory、Memori 内置、Honcho、LanceDB 引擎；Memory Wiki；第三方插件（Mem0、Hindsight） 它本身就是提供方：hermes plugins install hindsight 或 @vectorize-io/hindsight-openclaw

Hermes 如何处理记忆

Hermes 把始终在线的部分保持得很小。agent 通过记忆工具添加、替换或删除简短的条目。如果某次写入会超出上限，就返回错误，让 agent 先做整理。Hermes 文档 解释了冻结快照：它“保留 LLM 的前缀缓存”，所以系统提示在会话中途不会变化，缓存的 token 也保持便宜。

item.title: Claude Code Settings: Files, Precedence and Key Reference (2026)
item.description: Claude Code settings are JSON keys in a few files. Put a key in the file that matches who should get it, and the higher-ranked file wins when two files set the same key. This page covers where the files are, which one wins, the keys people change most, and how memory settings fit in. Facts come from the Claude Code settings docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/settings and /settings-reference), read on 10 November 2026.

item.title: Claude Code Skills: How They Work, Where They Live and Memory
item.description:
Claude Code skills are folders that hold a SKILL.md file with instructions for one kind of task. Claude reads each skill’s name and description at the start of a session. It loads the full instructions only when the task matches, or when you type /skill-name. Skills do not store facts about your work. For that, use CLAUDE.md files, auto memory, or a memory plugin.

This guide covers where skills live, the fields you can set, how they load, and what they do with memory. The source is the Claude Code skills docs, checked on 10 November 2026.

item.title: Codex CLI Config Reference: config.toml Keys and Defaults (2026)
item.description:
Codex CLI reads its settings from config.toml. The main file is ~/.codex/config.toml. Set a key there and every project uses it. Put a .codex/config.toml in a repo to change one project only. This page lists the keys people change most, their allowed values and defaults, using OpenAI’s configuration reference (checked 2026-11-10). Built-in memories are one key group; the Codex memory guide covers how they behave.

What is the Codex CLI config file?

The Codex CLI config file is a TOML file that sets the model, approval rules, sandbox, web search, memories, MCP servers and lifecycle hooks. OpenAI’s Config basics page says you copy only the keys you need into the file. Keys you leave out keep their built-in value, so a short file is normal.

item.title: OpenClaw 记忆：文件、搜索与嵌入模型
item.description:
OpenClaw 的记忆是一组文件。 agent 写下它要记住的内容，再读回来。MEMORY.md 存持久的事实和决定，USER.md 存你的偏好，按日期命名的每日笔记存正在进行的上下文。前两个文件在会话开始时加载。所有内容都会被存入 SQLite 建立索引，agent 通过 memory_search（向量搜索和关键词搜索的混合）找回更早的笔记。

OpenClaw 是开源（MIT）的个人 AI 助手，由 Peter Steinberger 和社区贡献者构建，现在由 OpenClaw Foundation 维护。它运行在你自己的电脑上，通过 WhatsApp、Telegram、Slack、Discord、iMessage 以及 20 多个其他渠道与你交流。本页内容来自官方记忆文档和记忆搜索文档，2026 年 10 月核对。第一次使用 OpenClaw？请先看 OpenClaw 指南，里面有安装、入门引导和 Gateway。

什么是 OpenClaw 记忆？

OpenClaw 记忆基于文件。 模型只能记住写到磁盘上、以 Markdown 形式保存在 agent 工作区里的内容。记忆插件（默认是 memory-core）为这些文件建立索引，并给 agent 提供搜索和读取它们的工具，所以知识在重启、压缩和新会话之后仍然保留。

因为记忆是纯文本，你可以像处理任何文件一样打开、编辑、对比和备份。这和把事实存在数据库里的记忆层不同。关于这类通用模式，参见 AI agent 记忆详解。

记忆文件

文件 存什么 何时加载
MEMORY.md 精选的长期事实和决定 会话开始时
USER.md（可选） 稳定的偏好、风格、人际关系、进行中的项目 会话开始时，预算较小
memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md 每日笔记和正在进行的上下文 在裸 /new 或 /reset 时加载今天和昨天的；其他时候通过搜索
memory/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md 带后缀的每日笔记，例如 session-memory 钩子生成的 同每日笔记
DREAMS.md（可选） 供人工审阅的 dreaming 摘要 不注入

工作区默认是 ~/.openclaw/workspace。如果 MEMORY.md 超过启动预算，磁盘上的文件保持完整，但注入的副本会被截断。/context list、/context detail 和 openclaw doctor 会显示大小和截断情况。

item.title: Hermes Agent Guide: Install, Setup, Memory and Plugins
item.description: Hermes Agent is an open-source AI agent from Nous Research that runs in your terminal and in chat apps such as Telegram, Discord and Slack. You can switch its model with one command, and it saves skills and notes from past work. Its built-in memory is two small text files plus a searchable log of past sessions. For a larger memory layer, you can add an external provider such as Hindsight.

item.title: Hermes Agent 指南：安装、设置、记忆与插件
item.description:
Hermes Agent 是 Nous Research 开发的开源 AI Agent。它在终端里运行，也能接入 Telegram、Discord、Slack 等聊天应用。你可以用一条命令切换模型，它还会把过去工作中的技能和笔记保存下来。它的内置记忆是两个很小的文本文件，加上一份可以搜索的历史会话记录。如果需要更大的记忆层，可以再接入外部提供商，比如 Hindsight。

本指南介绍安装、首次运行、消息网关和记忆。官方文档在 hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs。内容于 2026 年 11 月 10 日核对，最新版本为 v0.23.1（2026 年 11 月 10 日发布）。

什么是 Hermes Agent？

Hermes Agent 是一个会自我改进的 Agent，你可以把它运行在自己的电脑或服务器上。 它有终端界面（hermes 命令）、消息网关，以及一套技能系统：完成复杂任务后，它会写出可以复用的技能。它支持很多模型提供商，包括 Nous Portal、OpenRouter、OpenAI 和你自己的接口地址。官方 README 称，你可以"无需改代码、无锁定"地切换模型。

组成部分 作用 运行位置
终端界面 用 hermes 在终端里聊天 你的电脑
消息网关 一个进程，同时服务 Telegram、Discord、Slack、WhatsApp、Signal 和邮件 你的电脑或 VPS
终端后端 命令在哪里执行：本地、Docker、SSH、Modal、Daytona、Vercel Sandbox 本地或远程
桌面应用 基于同一份状态的原生应用，见 Hermes Agent 桌面版 你的电脑

如何安装 Hermes Agent？

只需运行一条命令。安装程序会装好 Hermes 需要的 Python、Node.js 和其他工具。

  1. Linux、macOS 或 WSL2： curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
  2. 原生 Windows： 运行安装页面上的 PowerShell 一行命令。文件放在 %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes 下。WSL2 安装使用 ~/.hermes，和 Linux 相同。
  3. Android（Termux）： 使用 Termux 指南和 APT 包，不用桌面脚本。
  4. 运行设置向导： hermes setup 一次完成所有配置。如果只想改模型，运行 hermes model。
  5. 开始聊天： 运行 hermes。要使用聊天应用，先运行 hermes gateway setup，再运行 hermes gateway start，然后给机器人发消息。

安装后常用的命令：hermes tools（开启或关闭工具）、hermes config set 和 hermes config get（读写单个设置），以及 hermes gateway（启动消息网关）。

item.title: OpenClaw Guide: Install, Onboarding, Gateway and Memory
item.description:
OpenClaw is an open-source AI assistant that runs on your own computer and talks to you through chat apps such as Telegram, Discord, Slack and WhatsApp. One process, the Gateway, runs the sessions, tools and chat connections. Its memory is plain Markdown files in the agent workspace. For months of history, you can add an external memory plugin such as Hindsight.

This guide covers the install, first run, the Gateway, and memory. The official docs are at docs.openclaw.ai. Checked on 9 November 2026, with the latest release at v2026.11.2 (8 November 2026).

item.title: OpenClaw 指南：安装、入门引导、Gateway 与记忆
item.description:
OpenClaw 是一个开源 AI 助手，运行在你自己的电脑上，通过 Telegram、Discord、Slack、WhatsApp 等聊天应用和你交流。一个叫 Gateway 的进程负责运行会话、工具和聊天连接。它的记忆是 agent 工作区里的纯 Markdown 文件。如果需要几个月的历史记录，可以再接入 Hindsight 这样的外部记忆插件。

本指南涵盖安装、首次运行、Gateway 和记忆。官方文档在 docs.openclaw.ai。内容核对于 2026 年 11 月 9 日，最新版本为 v2026.11.2（2026 年 11 月 8 日发布）。

OpenClaw 是什么？

OpenClaw 是一个你自己托管的个人 AI 助手，没有付费版，也没有托管服务。 它的 README 说，状态、记忆和凭证都留在你的硬件上。模型和 agent 框架（比如 Claude、Codex 或本地模型）都是插件，可以替换，不需要改动其他设置。

组成部分 作用 运行位置
Gateway 管理会话、工具、事件和聊天连接的控制中心 你的机器或服务器
控制界面、CLI、TUI 和 Gateway 对话、管理它的方式 你的机器
频道（Channels） WhatsApp、Telegram、Slack、Discord、Signal、iMessage 等聊天应用 连接到 Gateway
应用和节点 在支持的平台上提供语音、摄像头、屏幕和设备操作 手机、电脑

如何安装 OpenClaw？

安装脚本支持 macOS、Linux、WSL2 和 Windows。需要时，它会安装受支持的 Node.js 版本。

  1. macOS、Linux 或 WSL2： curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash
  2. Windows PowerShell： iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex
  3. 如果你自己管理 Node.js： npm install -g openclaw@latest。README 要求 24.x 系列使用 Node 24.16.0 或更新版本，或者 26.1.0 或更新版本；为了安全修复，它推荐 24.22.1+ 或 26.12.1+。如果 npm 是 11.15 或更旧的版本，去掉较新 npm 版本使用的 --allow-scripts=openclaw 参数。
  4. 完成入门引导： 安装脚本会自动启动它。通过包管理器安装后，运行 openclaw onboard --install-daemon。入门引导会检查模型访问、创建工作区并设置 Gateway。
  5. 检查并打开界面： 运行 openclaw gateway status，然后运行 openclaw dashboard。在控制界面发一条消息，确认助手会回复。

Docker、Nix 和其他安装方式，请看安装指南。

item.title: Is There a Standard Format for AI Agent Memory? (2026)
item.description: There is no standard format for AI agent memory as of November 2026. A note an agent saves in one tool stays in that tool’s shape: a Markdown file, a cited fact on GitHub’s servers, a labeled block, an extracted sentence with a user_id, a JSONL knowledge graph. Three open proposals try to fix that. None has real adoption yet, so sharing memory between agents today means picking one place all of them can reach.

item.title: Claude Dreaming: Managed Agents Memory Stores and Dreams
item.description:
Claude dreaming is an offline memory pass: Claude rereads past session transcripts and its own memory notes, corrects notes that turned out wrong, merges duplicates, and builds new structures such as a wiki or an index that later sessions can navigate. Anthropic described it in The components of agent memory (November 6, 2026) and ships it in Claude Managed Agents as Dreams, a research-preview API.

This page explains what Anthropic means by agent memory, how memory stores and Dreams work, what the published tests showed (CL-Bench, Pokémon Red, a 420M-token wiki), and how the approach compares with Letta’s dreaming and Hindsight’s background consolidation. Every number comes from Anthropic’s post, its docs or its cookbook, and none of it was reproduced here.

item.title: Everything Claude Code (ECC) Memory and Instincts
item.description:
ECC (Everything Claude Code) gives Claude Code memory through three local layers: hooks that save a session summary and reload it next time, instincts (small learned habits with confidence scores) built from your sessions, and a Memory Vault of Markdown handoffs shared across agents. Instinct learning is off by default, and ECC publishes no memory benchmarks.

ECC lives at affaan-m/ECC: MIT, created January 2026, 294,084 GitHub stars on 1 November 2026 (GitHub API). The current release is 2.2.3 (1 October 2026), also on npm as ecc-universal. It bundles 71 agents, 314 skills, 98 command shims, hooks, rules and a security scanner, per its README. This page covers only the memory part, from the README, the continuous-learning-v2 skill, the hooks docs and the Memory Vault design doc, read 1 November 2026. For the wider picture, see AI coding agent memory.

item.title: CodeGraph: Code Knowledge Graph for Claude Code and Codex
item.description:
CodeGraph is an open-source CLI and MCP server that turns a codebase into a local code knowledge graph, so a coding agent asks one question and gets back the relevant source and call paths instead of grepping and reading files one by one. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Hermes Agent and more. It remembers the code’s structure, not what happened in past sessions.

The repo is colbymchenry/codegraph: MIT, TypeScript with a Rust parsing kernel, created January 2026, 76,051 GitHub stars on 31 October 2026 (GitHub API). The latest release is v1.6.2 (3 October 2026), also on npm as @colbymchenry/codegraph. Facts below come from its README and docs site, checked 31 October 2026. For the wider picture, see AI coding agent memory.

item.title: Headroom: Context Compression for Claude Code and Codex
item.description:
Headroom is an open-source tool that shrinks what an AI coding agent reads (tool outputs, logs, files, RAG chunks and history) before it reaches the model, so the same work uses fewer tokens and less of the context window. It runs locally as a proxy, library or MCP server and wraps Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Aider and others in one command.

The repo is headroomlabs-ai/headroom: Apache-2.0, created January 2026, 78,458 GitHub stars on 31 October 2026 (GitHub API). The latest release on PyPI is headroom-ai 0.42.0 (26 October 2026). Facts below come from its README and docs, checked 31 October 2026. For the general techniques, see LLM memory compression.

item.title: What Is Context Engineering? Techniques and Memory
item.description: Context engineering is the work of choosing which tokens an AI agent sees at each step: instructions, tool definitions, retrieved documents, memories and the parts of past turns that still matter. It exists because models get worse as their context fills up. The techniques fall into a few groups: add the right information, cut what’s stale, compress history, split work across clean contexts, and store the rest outside the window.

item.title: Grok Bot Memory: How xAI's Bots Remember, and Plugins
item.description:
Grok Bot memory is per Bot. xAI’s docs say each Bot keeps “stable working preferences, important facts, and summaries from its work”, separate from your other Bots. Bots share a cloud computer, a skill library and connected apps, but not learned memory. For memory shared across Bots and other tools, you add a plugin such as Hindsight, Supermemory or claude-mem.

Everything below comes from xAI’s Grok Bot docs, the launch post and each plugin’s own documentation, checked on October 24, 2026. Grok Bot is still in beta, so details may change.

item.title: Hermes Agent Desktop: Install, Memory and Setup
item.description:
Hermes Agent Desktop is the official native app for Nous Research’s Hermes Agent, for macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows and Linux. It isn’t a separate agent: it runs the same core as the hermes CLI and reads the same config, sessions, skills and memory. Install it from the Hermes website, or run hermes desktop if the CLI is already installed.

Hermes Agent is MIT-licensed and had about 256,500 GitHub stars on October 24, 2026. Everything below comes from the official Hermes Desktop docs and installation guide, checked October 2026, with Hermes at v0.22.5.

item.title: Hermes Agent Desktop：安装、记忆与设置
item.description:
Hermes Agent Desktop 是 Nous Research 的 Hermes Agent 官方原生应用，支持 macOS（Apple Silicon）、Windows 和 Linux。它不是另一个 Agent：底层运行的是和 hermes 命令行相同的核心，读取的是同一套配置、会话、技能和记忆。你可以从 Hermes 官网安装，如果已经装了命令行，也可以直接运行 hermes desktop。

Hermes Agent 使用 MIT 许可证，2026 年 10 月 24 日在 GitHub 上约有 256,500 颗星。下面的内容都来自官方的 Hermes Desktop 文档 和 安装指南，2026 年 10 月核对，当时 Hermes 版本为 v0.22.5。

什么是 Hermes Agent Desktop？

Hermes Agent Desktop 是一个 Electron 应用，在标准 Hermes Agent 运行时之上提供一个以聊天为主的窗口。 用 Nous Research 的话说，它使用的是“与命令行相同的配置、相同的 API 密钥、相同的会话、相同的技能、相同的记忆”，并且“不是一个单独的产品，也不是轻量克隆”。

Nous Research 于 2026 年 6 月 2 日以 v0.15.2 公开预览版的形式发布了它，Decrypt 报道过此事。应用默认会启动并管理自己的本地后端。它也可以连接到另一台机器上的 Hermes 后端（比如 VPS、家用服务器，或者通过 Tailscale 连接的 Mac mini），前提是那台机器上已经运行了 hermes serve。应用不会替你启动它。

item.title: OpenViking: ByteDance's Context Database for Agent Memory
item.description: OpenViking is an open-source context database for AI agents from the Viking team at ByteDance’s Volcengine. It keeps everything an agent knows (documents, long-term memories and skills) in one virtual filesystem under viking://, writes a short summary for every directory, and lets agents read context with file commands like ls, tree, find and grep. Memories come from sessions: when a chat is committed, OpenViking extracts them in the background as Markdown files you can open and edit.

item.title: Voice Agent Memory: How Voice AI Remembers Callers
item.description:
How does voice agent memory work?

Voice agent memory keeps facts about a caller between calls and puts the relevant ones in front of the model before it speaks. A memory store keyed to the caller saves each call’s content in the background. On the next call, the agent recalls only what matters to this turn, inside a latency budget of a few hundred milliseconds.

A stock voice pipeline (speech-to-text, LLM, text-to-speech) starts every call with an empty context. When the caller hangs up, everything they said is gone. Pasting old transcripts into the prompt doesn’t scale: the prompt grows with every call, and a longer prompt delays the first spoken word.

item.title: Hermes Agent Plugins: Install, Catalog, Memory Providers
item.description:
Hermes Agent plugins are folders of Python code with a plugin.yaml manifest that add tools, hooks, slash commands, memory backends and other features without changing Hermes’s core. You install them with hermes plugins install <name> from a human-reviewed, commit-pinned catalog, or from any Git repo. Memory provider plugins are a special kind: only one runs at a time.

Hermes Agent is Nous Research’s open-source (MIT) agent, with about 256,000 GitHub stars on October 21, 2026. This page covers the plugin system: plugin types, install commands, the catalog, how memory providers hook in, and which ones exist. For how Hermes’s built-in memory works (MEMORY.md, USER.md, session search), see Hermes Agent memory. Facts come from the Hermes plugin docs and the repo’s plugin-catalog/ folder, checked October 21, 2026.

item.title: Hermes Agent Skills: How Procedural Memory Works
item.description:
Hermes Agent skills are the agent’s procedural memory: markdown files that record how to do a task. Hermes writes them itself after working out a multi-step job, patches them when it hits a new pitfall, and loads one only when a task needs it. Each skill is a SKILL.md folder under ~/.hermes/skills/, in the open Agent Skills format.

Hermes Agent is the MIT-licensed agent from Nous Research, with about 256,000 GitHub stars on 21 October 2026. This page covers how its skills are made, stored, loaded, shared and cleaned up. Facts come from the official Skills System docs, the Curator docs and the v0.22 release notes, checked 21 October 2026. For the fact files and session search, see Hermes Agent memory.

item.title: Hermes Agent 技能：程序性记忆如何工作
item.description:
Hermes Agent 技能是 agent 的程序性记忆：记录怎么完成一项任务的 markdown 文件。Hermes 在完成一项多步骤工作后自己写出技能，遇到新的坑时修改它，任务需要时才加载某一个。每个技能是 ~/.hermes/skills/ 下的一个 SKILL.md 文件夹，采用开放的 Agent Skills 格式。

Hermes Agent 是 Nous Research 开发的 MIT 许可证 agent，2026 年 10 月 21 日在 GitHub 上约有 256,000 颗星。本页说明它的技能如何产生、存放、加载、分享和清理。内容来自官方的 Skills System 文档、Curator 文档 以及 v0.22 发行说明，2026 年 10 月 21 日核对。关于事实文件和会话搜索，见 Hermes Agent 记忆。

Hermes Agent 技能是什么？

Hermes 技能是一个带 SKILL.md 文件的文件夹：开头是 YAML 前置信息（name、description、version、tags），正文写明何时使用、步骤、坑点和如何检查结果。agent 能看到每个技能的名称和描述，只有任务匹配时才读取完整文件。

文档说得很直接：agent “整理出一个非简单的工作流程时，会把这个方法保存为技能，供以后重复使用”。这就是技能和记忆的区别。记忆说的是什么是真的（“用户在太平洋时区”）。技能说的是怎么做一件事（“如何部署到 Kubernetes”）。Hermes 指南给出的经验法则是：“如果你会把它放进参考文档，它就是技能。如果你会把它写在便利贴上，它就是记忆。”

技能并不是 Hermes 独有的。这种格式遵循 Agent Skills 规范，Claude Code、Codex 等工具也读取它，所以一个技能文件夹可以在不同工具之间搬用。Hermes 的不同之处在于围绕它的循环：agent 自己写和改技能，后台任务还会清理没人用的技能。更广义的概念见英文页面 procedural memory in AI agents。

item.title: Hermes Agent 插件：安装、目录与记忆提供方
item.description:
Hermes Agent 插件是包含 plugin.yaml 清单的 Python 代码文件夹。它们可以添加工具、钩子、斜杠命令、记忆后端等功能，而不需要改动 Hermes 的核心。你可以用 hermes plugins install <名称> 从经人工审核、固定提交的目录中安装，也可以从任意 Git 仓库安装。记忆提供方插件比较特殊：同一时间只有一个在运行。

Hermes Agent 是 Nous Research 推出的开源（MIT）agent，截至 2026 年 10 月 21 日在 GitHub 上约有 256,000 颗星。本页介绍插件系统：插件类型、安装命令、目录、记忆提供方如何接入，以及有哪些提供方。Hermes 内置记忆如何工作（MEMORY.md、USER.md、会话搜索）见 Hermes Agent 记忆。事实来自 Hermes 插件文档 以及仓库中的 plugin-catalog/ 文件夹，2026 年 10 月 21 日核对。

什么是 Hermes Agent 插件？

Hermes 插件是一个目录，里面有 plugin.yaml 清单和一个定义了 register(ctx) 的 __init__.py。Hermes 启动时会调用这个函数，插件通过 ctx 注册模型可以调用的工具、生命周期钩子、斜杠命令、CLI 子命令、随附的技能，或者像记忆存储这样的后端。

用户插件放在 ~/.hermes/plugins/<名称>/。Hermes 还会在仓库的 plugins/ 文件夹中发现内置插件、暴露 hermes_agent.plugins 入口点的 pip 包，以及 NixOS 模块配置中声明的插件。项目本地的 ./.hermes/plugins/ 文件夹不会被加载：文档说，运行每个会话的网关每个进程只发现一次插件，而不是每个工作目录发现一次。

item.title: AI Agent Memory Statistics (October 2026)
item.description:
These AI agent memory statistics were collected on 2026-10-20 by aiagentmemory.org from the GitHub, PyPI and npm APIs. claude-mem has the most GitHub stars (101,934), Mem0 has the most PyPI downloads (2,020,516 last month), and Hindsight ranks fourth on stars and second on PyPI downloads. Hindsight had the top BEAM 10M score in MemTensor’s same-model OmniMemEval run (59.75, checked 2026-10-12).

All GitHub and download numbers on this page were collected 2026-10-20 between about 18:45 and 18:56 UTC, by us, from public APIs. We’re the primary source for them. Benchmark scores are not ours: they’re copied from the vendors who ran them, with who ran each one. The exact calls are in the Methodology section.

item.title: Hindsight Memlake vs Postgres, turbopuffer and LanceDB
item.description:
Hindsight Memlake is an object-storage engine built only for agent memory, sitting under Hindsight’s extraction, consolidation and recall. Postgres with pgvector, turbopuffer, LanceDB and Pinecone serverless are general retrieval stores you build memory on yourself. In Vectorize-run benchmarks Memlake beats Hindsight’s own Postgres backend by a wide margin on large banks, but it’s Enterprise only, and for banks under ~50k memories Vectorize says Postgres is fine.

So the comparison is partly apples to oranges. This page compares them where they do overlap (where the data lives, how writes become visible, which searches run on one copy, cold start, licensing) using each vendor’s own docs, checked on 20 October 2026. No benchmark here is invented, and no head-to-head between Memlake and turbopuffer, LanceDB or Pinecone exists.

item.title: Mnemosyne vs Hindsight: Agent Memory Compared
item.description:
Mnemosyne vs Hindsight is a choice between a small local library and a full memory server. Mnemosyne is one pip install and one SQLite file, built first for Hermes Agent, and runs on a Raspberry Pi. Hindsight runs as a server on PostgreSQL, searches four ways at once, and consolidates facts into observations it can reason over with reflect.

On benchmarks, Mnemosyne’s own README puts Hindsight ahead: 73.4% to 65.2% on BEAM at 100K, with a judge-model caveat. Mnemosyne publishes no end-to-end score on longer histories, where Hindsight reports 73.9 at 1M and 64.1 at 10M tokens. This page compares the two on storage, recall, setup, benchmarks and limits, from each project’s README and docs, checked on 20 October 2026.

item.title: Cline Memory Bank: Files, Setup, Cost and Limits
item.description:
The Cline Memory Bank is a set of custom instructions that make Cline keep six markdown files in your repository and read all of them at the start of every task. It is documentation the agent maintains itself, not a memory store: nothing is embedded, nothing is searched, and the whole folder re-enters the context window on each task.

Every fact below comes from Cline’s Memory Bank docs, its prompting guide and Cline’s own announcement post, checked on 18 October 2026.

item.title: claude-mem: How It Works, Install, Cost and Limits
item.description:
claude-mem is an Apache 2.0 plugin that gives a coding agent memory of its own past sessions. Lifecycle hooks capture what the agent does, an LLM compresses that into observations and summaries, a local worker stores them in SQLite, and the next session starts with the relevant parts already in context.

It is one of the most starred agent memory projects on GitHub: 114,617 stars on 8 November 2026 (103,771 on 28 October), from a repo created on 31 August 2025 by Alex Newman (@thedotmack). Every fact below comes from the claude-mem README and docs.claude-mem.ai, checked on 17 October 2026 (the install and trial wording re-read on 8 November); the release changes through v15.12.0 come from the release notes, checked on 8 November 2026. For Claude Code’s own built-in memory, which is a separate thing, see Claude Code memory.

item.title: GitHub Copilot Memory: What It Stores and Where
item.description:
Copilot Memory is GitHub’s automatic memory for Copilot’s agentic features. It saves two things as Copilot works: repository facts (conventions, architecture decisions, build commands) and user preferences. Each fact stores citations to the code that supports it, Copilot revalidates those citations before using the fact, votes on whether it still holds, and anything that goes 90 days without an upvote expires.

It became generally available on paid Copilot plans on 28 October 2026, per GitHub’s changelog, which also added VS Code, the Copilot app, GitHub Mobile, Slack and Teams as surfaces and introduced Copilot dreaming in public preview. Every fact below comes from GitHub’s Copilot Memory docs, its how-to pages and that changelog, read on 9 November 2026. Two numbers changed since this page was first written in October: the expiry went from 28 days to 90, and the surface list went from four to eight. For how other agents handle the same problem, see AI coding agent memory.

item.title: Agent Memory vs Documentation: Which Does Your Agent Need?
item.description:
Use both, for different jobs. Documentation is curated knowledge a human wrote and reviews: requirements, decisions, constraints. Agent memory is an automatic record of what happened across sessions, including the failures nobody would ever write down. Docs answer “what should this be?”; memory answers “what did we already try?”

What the agent memory vs documentation debate is about

In October 2026 a post titled “Agents don’t need memory, they need documentation” by Kevin Liao reached 392 points on Hacker News. It argued that memory plugins all share one shape (generate snippets from transcripts, store them in a vector database, inject the top matches) and that this shape is broken for coding work.

item.title: Graphify: Codebase Knowledge Graph Memory for Agents
item.description:
Graphify is an open-source skill and CLI that maps a codebase, with its docs, PDFs and media, into a knowledge graph that a coding agent queries instead of grepping files. Code is parsed locally with tree-sitter, with no LLM. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and 20+ other assistants. It remembers the code’s structure, not what happened in past sessions.

The repo is Graphify-Labs/graphify: Apache-2.0, created April 2026, about 126,500 GitHub stars on 15 October 2026. The PyPI package is graphifyy (double y). Facts below come from its README and BENCHMARKS.md, checked 15 October 2026. For the wider picture of memory in coding tools, see AI coding agent memory.

item.title: Codex Memory: AGENTS.md, Memories and Add-ons
item.description:
Codex memory is two built-in layers. AGENTS.md files hold instructions you write, and Codex loads them at the start of every run. Codex memories, off by default, turn useful context from past chats into local files under ~/.codex/memories/. For memory that is searchable, shared across agents or kept on a server, add a hook-based plugin such as Hindsight.

Codex is OpenAI’s coding agent for the terminal, IDE and ChatGPT desktop app. Each session starts with an empty context window, so anything Codex should know must come back in from a file or a tool. Facts below come from OpenAI’s Codex memories docs and AGENTS.md guide, checked 13 October 2026, and from the Codex source and release notes up to 0.167.0 (6 November 2026). For Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot, see AI coding agent memory.

item.title: DeepSeek Harness Memory: Sessions, Compaction, Plugins
item.description:
DeepSeek Harness memory has two built-in parts: an append-only session log that is the source of everything the model sees, and automatic compaction that summarizes old history when the context fills. Neither survives into a new session. For memory across sessions, you add a plugin (Hindsight, Honcho, Mem0, ReMe, Nowledge Mem, dsh-mnemon) or an MCP memory server.

DeepSeek Harness (dsh) is DeepSeek’s open-source agent harness: MIT-licensed, written in TypeScript, built on the Cordis plugin framework (“Everything is a Plugin”), and still a developer preview with breaking changes expected. It launched on GitHub on 13 August 2026 and had about 258,000 stars on 22 October 2026. Facts below come from its README, architecture doc and MCP memory guide, plus each plugin’s own docs, checked 13 October 2026. For Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, see AI coding agent memory.

item.title: Oracle AI Agent Memory: SDK, Setup, Limits
item.description:
Oracle AI Agent Memory is Oracle’s memory SDK for AI agents, installed with pip install oracleagentmemory. It stores conversation threads, summaries and long-term memories inside Oracle AI Database, extracts memories from chats with an LLM, and retrieves them with vector, keyword or hybrid search. It suits teams that already run Oracle and want agent memory under the same governance.

What is Oracle AI Agent Memory?

Oracle AI Agent Memory is a model- and framework-agnostic Python library that turns Oracle AI Database into an agent memory store. Oracle’s docs call it “the governed memory core in the AI agents ecosystem.” Short-term memory lives in threads with summaries and context cards. Long-term memory holds user preferences, learned rules and facts across sessions.

item.title: Agent Memory Leaderboard: Benchmarks and Scores
item.description:
There is no official agent memory leaderboard. The benchmark authors (LongMemEval, LoCoMo, BEAM) publish datasets, not rankings. The leaderboards you can find are run by memory vendors: agentmemorybenchmark.ai by Vectorize, the company that makes Hindsight; OmniMemEval by MemTensor, the company that makes MemOS; and score pages from Mem0, Zep, Honcho and past.dev.

So every ranking has an owner, and every score depends on the answer model, judge and token budget that owner chose. This page lists where the leaderboards are, what each benchmark measures, the published scores with who reported each one, and how to read them. Everything was checked on the source pages on 12 October 2026. For GitHub stars and PyPI and npm download counts for 23 memory projects, see AI agent memory statistics.

item.title: Agent Workflow Memory (2026): Paper Results, Limits and Code
item.description:
Agent workflow memory means an LLM agent keeps reusable routines learned from its own past runs and follows them on new tasks. The best-known version is Agent Workflow Memory (AWM) by Wang, Mao, Fried and Neubig (CMU and MIT, ICML 2025). AWM induces workflows from past trajectories and puts the relevant ones in the agent’s prompt.

On web navigation with GPT-4, the paper reports WebArena task success of 35.5% against 23.5% for the BrowserGym agent, and Mind2Web step success of 45.1% against 36.2% for MindAct. Later work found the gain shrinks or disappears with newer models. This page explains how AWM builds workflows, the difference between its online and offline modes, the full results, the limits found by the authors and by later work, and how to build workflow memory into an agent today. Sources: the arXiv paper, the ICML 2025 proceedings version, and the official repo, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: agentmemory: Persistent Memory for AI Coding Agents
item.description:
agentmemory is an open-source memory server that gives AI coding agents persistent memory across sessions. Hooks in Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw and other agents record what the agent does, and the server injects the most relevant past context when the next session starts. You install it with npx -y @agentmemory/agentmemory@latest.

The project lives at github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory, is written in TypeScript under the Apache 2.0 license, and had about 29,900 GitHub stars on 26 October 2026 (29,300 on 12 October). This page covers what it does, how it works, how to set it up, what its benchmark numbers mean, and how it compares with Hindsight and Mem0 for coding-agent memory. Facts come from the agentmemory README and benchmark files, checked on 12 October 2026. (This site, aiagentmemory.org, has no connection to the agentmemory project.)

item.title: Claude Code Memory: CLAUDE.md, Auto Memory and Plugins
item.description:
Claude Code memory is two built-in systems. CLAUDE.md files hold instructions you write, and Claude Code loads them at the start of every session. Auto memory holds notes Claude writes for itself in ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/. You manage both with /memory. For more than notes, add a memory MCP server or a plugin such as claude-mem or Hindsight.

Each Claude Code session starts with an empty context window, so anything Claude should know has to come from a file that loads back in. This page covers how Claude Code’s built-in memory works, from Anthropic’s Claude Code memory docs, then the add-on options and how they compare. All facts were checked on 12 October 2026. For how other coding agents (Cursor, Copilot) handle memory, see AI coding agent memory, or GitHub Copilot Memory for Copilot’s citation-checked repository facts in detail. The Claude chat app at claude.ai has its own, separate memory feature, covered in Claude AI long-term memory.

item.title: TencentDB Agent Memory (v2.0.3): Layers, Team Memory, Setup
item.description:
TencentDB Agent Memory (repo TencentDB-Agent-Memory) is an open-source memory hub for AI agents from Tencent Cloud Database. It sits as a proxy between a coding agent and its LLM, saves each conversation, distills it into four layers (L0 to L3), and injects the right memory, skills, docs and code knowledge into every request. Its Team Memory release lets several agents and people share those assets with access control.

It is MIT-licensed, written mostly in TypeScript, and had about 30,080 GitHub stars on 29 October 2026, up from 29,600 on 19 October. This page covers how its memory layers work, how to install it, what Team Memory adds, which agents it supports, and how it compares with Hindsight and Mem0. Facts come from the project’s README, INSTALL.md, CHANGELOG.md, the GitHub releases list and the SDK README, rechecked on 19 October 2026; the 2.0.3 section comes from the v2.0.3 release notes, read on 29 October 2026.

item.title: Mem0 vs MemPalace: Extracted Facts vs Verbatim Recall
item.description:
Mem0 vs MemPalace is a choice between keeping facts and keeping everything. Mem0 sends each conversation to an LLM, pulls out short facts like “prefers Go,” and returns the matching ones on search. MemPalace saves conversations and files word for word on your machine and finds them later with local search, with no LLM and no API key.

Both are open source and among the most-starred memory projects on GitHub. They solve different problems: Mem0 is a memory layer for apps with many users, MemPalace is a personal, local archive built mostly for coding agents. Hindsight, an MIT memory server, covers ground from both: per-user banks for apps, native plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, a fully local mode, and the top answer-accuracy scores of the three on LongMemEval and BEAM. Facts below come from each project’s README, docs and PyPI page, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: Mem0 vs Honcho: User Modeling, Self-Hosting and Benchmarks
item.description:
Mem0 vs Honcho is a choice between remembering facts and understanding people. Mem0 pulls short facts out of conversations and returns the ones that match a query. Honcho keeps the full messages, runs background reasoning over them, and builds a model of each participant that your agent can ask questions about in plain language.

Both are open source and both have a managed service. They differ in license (Apache 2.0 vs AGPL-3.0), in how much LLM work happens after each write, and in how they treat multi-agent conversations. Many teams weighing the two also look at Hindsight, an MIT-licensed memory server that, like Honcho, reasons over memories in the background, and posts the highest vendor-reported scores of the three on LongMemEval and BEAM. Sources are each project’s README, docs, pricing page and published evals, checked on 12 October 2026; the self-hosting facts were rechecked on 29 October 2026.

item.title: Mem0 vs Supermemory: Agent Memory APIs Compared
item.description:
Mem0 vs Supermemory is a choice between a memory-only layer and a memory-plus-context API. Mem0 extracts short facts from conversations and returns them by hybrid search, and you can run all of it yourself. Supermemory does fact extraction too, but bundles it with user profiles, document RAG and data connectors behind one hosted API.

Both have a free tier (since 26 October 2026 Mem0’s needs your own LLM key after 30 days, and its paid plans are custom; Supermemory’s paid plans start at $19/month), and both can run on your machine, though in very different ways. Many teams comparing the two also look at Hindsight, an MIT-licensed memory server that scores highest of the three on LongMemEval and leads Mem0 by 9.8 and 15.5 points on the long-history BEAM 1M and 10M tests. This page compares all three on memory model, retrieval, self-hosting, benchmarks and pricing, using each project’s README, docs and pricing pages and Mem0’s own comparison pages, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: Mem0 vs Hindsight: Agent Memory Layers Compared
item.description:
Mem0 vs Hindsight is a choice between two memory layers that sit beside your agent, not inside it. Hindsight does more work per memory: it links entities and time, merges facts into observations in the background, and can reason over them with reflect. Mem0 keeps memory lean: one LLM pass extracts facts, and search returns a small set of them cheaply.

The data splits along that line. On Mem0’s own comparison page, Hindsight leads by 9.8 points on BEAM 1M and 15.5 points on BEAM 10M, the long-history tests, and ships graph, temporal recall and consolidation in its MIT release, where Mem0 keeps them on its paid Platform. Mem0 returns about 4x fewer tokens per retrieval and lists SOC 2 and HIPAA for its Platform. This page compares them on memory model, retrieval, what’s free versus paid, benchmarks and cost, using each project’s README, docs and pricing pages, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: AI Memory Injection: How Agent Memory Gets Poisoned
item.description:
AI memory injection is an attack that gets malicious instructions or false facts saved into an AI agent’s long-term memory, so they keep influencing the agent in later sessions. Unlike a one-off prompt injection, the bad entry persists. In shared memory it can reach other users. OWASP lists it as ASI06: Memory and Context Poisoning in its 2026 agentic Top 10.

This page explains how memory injection works, the main published attacks, and the defenses that hold up. The term has a second, harmless meaning too, covered at the end.

item.title: AI Memory Decay: How and Why Agents Forget
item.description:
AI memory decay is the gradual loss of a stored memory’s influence on an agent, either by design or by accident. Designed decay is a scoring rule that makes old or unused memories less likely to be retrieved. Accidental decay is what happens when information falls out of the context window, gets buried in a long prompt, or is lost in a summary.

The first kind is a feature you tune. The second is a bug you work around. This page covers both, with the formulas used in published systems and the evidence for each.

item.title: How to Add Memory to a Chatbot (with Python)
item.description:
To add memory to a chatbot, store each conversation’s messages and resend them with every request, then trim or summarize old turns so the history fits the model’s window. For memory across conversations, also save key facts about the user to a database and add the relevant ones to the prompt when a new chat starts.

What is chatbot memory?

Chatbot memory is everything an app sends to the model so it can respond as if it remembers: the recent message history of the current chat (short-term memory) and stored facts from past chats (long-term memory). The model itself keeps nothing. Every API request starts blank unless your code puts the past back in.

item.title: Microsoft Memora: Agent Memory With Cue Anchors
item.description:
Microsoft Memora is a research memory system for AI agents from Microsoft Research. Its idea is to separate what is stored from how it is found: each memory keeps its full detail, but search runs only over a short summary (the primary abstraction) and a few tags (cue anchors). The paper was accepted at ICML 2026 and the code is MIT-licensed on GitHub.

This page explains how Memora works, what Microsoft reports about its results, how to try it, and where it sits next to production memory tools. Sources are the arXiv paper, the Microsoft Research blog post (June 29, 2026) and the microsoft/Memora repository.

item.title: Holographic Memory for AI Agents: HRR Explained
item.description:
Holographic memory for AI agents means storing facts as holographic reduced representations (HRR): vectors bound together with circular convolution and added into one fixed-size vector, then pulled back out by unbinding with a cue. The idea dates from Tony Plate’s 1995 paper. The main working example in agents is the Holographic memory provider in Hermes Agent.

The name sounds futuristic, and many pages online treat it as a vague vision of “multi-dimensional recall”. It isn’t. HRR is a specific, small piece of math with known strengths and a known capacity limit. This page explains both, and what it looks like inside a real agent.

item.title: Supermemory: Long-Term AI Memory as a Service
item.description:
Supermemory is long-term memory sold as a service: one API that extracts facts from conversations, keeps a profile for each user, and searches your documents and those memories together. You send content scoped to a user or project, and Supermemory handles chunking, embeddings, extraction, contradictions and forgetting. It also runs locally as a single binary.

This page covers what Supermemory does, how its memory model works, the current Python SDK, the local server, pricing and its benchmark claims. Sources are the Supermemory GitHub README, the docs and the pricing page, checked on 8 October 2026.

item.title: Honcho Memory (2026): Self-Hosting, Pricing, v3.5.0
item.description:
Honcho is an open-source memory service for LLM agents, built by Plastic Labs. Instead of only storing extracted facts, it reasons about the people and agents in your conversations. You save messages; a background worker derives conclusions about each participant; then you ask Honcho what it knows, in plain language or as prompt-ready context.

In short: Honcho memory is a peer model, not a fact list. It is AGPL-3.0, self-hostable on Postgres with pgvector, priced at $2 per million ingested tokens on the managed service, and built into Hermes Agent as a memory provider. The current server is 3.5.0 (30 October 2026).

item.title: How Does Memory Work in AI? Write, Store, Retrieve, Inject
item.description:
AI memory works by saving information outside the model and adding it back into the prompt later. The language model forgets everything after each reply. So the app around it writes notes or keeps past chats, searches them when you send a new message, and pastes the relevant pieces into the model’s input. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and custom agents all follow this loop.

What is AI memory?

AI memory is the ability of an AI system to use information from earlier conversations or tasks in a new one, by storing that information outside the model and retrieving the relevant parts when needed. It’s a feature of the app or agent, not of the model. The model sees only what’s in its current input; memory decides what goes there.

item.title: Spring AI Chat Memory: ChatMemory, Advisors, JDBC
item.description:
Spring AI conversational memory is handled by the ChatMemory interface and a memory advisor on the ChatClient. MessageWindowChatMemory keeps the last 20 messages per conversation by default. A ChatMemoryRepository stores them in memory, JDBC, Cassandra, Neo4j, MongoDB or Redis. MessageChatMemoryAdvisor adds that history to every prompt.

This page follows the Spring AI 2.0.x chat memory reference. Spring AI 2.0.0 shipped in June 2026 and changed memory behavior in ways that break 1.x code; those changes are covered below. Spring AI is a Java framework, so the examples are Java.

item.title: Hindsight AI Memory: How It Works and When to Use It
item.description:
Hindsight is an open-source agent memory server from Vectorize, released under the MIT license with the full server included. It gives an AI agent three operations: retain (store and extract facts), recall (search memories) and reflect (reason over them to answer a question). It runs on PostgreSQL with pgvector, self-hosted or as the managed Hindsight Cloud.

Its strongest case is long histories: on the BEAM benchmark it scores 73.9 at 1M tokens and 64.1 at 10M, 9.8 and 15.5 points ahead of Mem0 by Mem0’s own comparison page. It also ships every feature (graph, temporal recall, consolidation, mental models, reflect) in the open-source release. This page covers how it works, what the benchmarks show, its real limits, and when another tool is the better pick. Facts come from the GitHub README, the official docs and the paper, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: Letta vs LangChain Memory: Harness vs Library (2026)
item.description:
Letta vs LangChain memory is a choice between a harness and a library. Letta runs the agent for you and lets it edit its own memory, stored as git-backed Markdown files. LangChain gives you Python building blocks: a LangGraph checkpointer for chat history and a store for long-term facts. Your code decides what goes in.

Older comparisons describe Letta as a Python server with memory blocks and LangChain as ConversationBufferMemory. Both pictures are out of date. Letta retired its Python API server in 2026, and LangChain deprecated its memory classes. This page compares what each ships as of October 2026.

item.title: Mem0 vs Cognee: User Memory vs Knowledge Graph
item.description:
Mem0 vs Cognee is a choice between two memory shapes. Mem0 extracts short facts from conversations and stores them per user for personalization. Cognee turns documents, code and conversations into a knowledge graph plus vector index that agents search. Both are Apache 2.0 and self-hostable, but only Cognee keeps graph memory in its open-source version.

A third option many teams weigh here is Hindsight, an MIT-licensed memory server that, like Cognee, keeps graph and temporal recall in open source, but stores everything in PostgreSQL and is built around per-user conversation memory like Mem0. It leads Mem0 by 9.8 and 15.5 points on the long-history BEAM 1M and 10M tests in Mem0’s own comparison.

item.title: Mem0 vs Letta: Memory Layer or Stateful Agent?
item.description:
Mem0 vs Letta comes down to one question: do you want a memory service for an agent you already have, or a runtime where the agent manages its own memory? Mem0 is a memory layer your code calls with add and search. Letta (formerly MemGPT) is a stateful agent harness whose agents read, edit and consolidate their own memory files.

The two are often listed side by side, but they sit at different levels of the stack. A third option, Hindsight, sits between them: a memory layer like Mem0 that you call from any agent, but one that consolidates and reasons over memories in the background, the way Letta’s agents do, all under MIT. This page compares them on memory model, control, language support, hosting and cost, using each project’s README, docs and pricing page as of 12 October 2026.

item.title: LLM Memory With Obsidian: Karpathy's LLM Wiki Pattern
item.description:
Using Obsidian as LLM memory means letting an AI agent write and maintain a folder of linked Markdown notes that you browse in Obsidian. The best-known version is Andrej Karpathy’s LLM Wiki, published as a gist in April 2026. You drop sources into a folder, the agent compiles them into wiki pages, and both of you read the wiki instead of re-searching raw documents.

This page explains what Karpathy actually proposed, how to set it up with Obsidian, the tools that help it scale, and when a memory server fits better. The main source is Karpathy’s LLM Wiki gist, dated April 4, 2026.

item.title: Knowledge Graphs for AI Agent Memory: How They Work
item.description:
A knowledge graph memory stores what an AI agent learns as entities (a user, a company, a product) connected by relationships (“works at”, “prefers”, “reported bug in”). An LLM extracts those entities and relationships from conversations and documents, and the agent later retrieves facts by searching the graph and following its links. The graph makes connections and changes explicit, which flat vector memory can’t do.

This page explains how graph memory is built, how retrieval works, the main tools (Graphiti, Neo4j Agent Memory, Cognee, Hindsight, GraphRAG), and when a graph beats a vector store.

item.title: MemPalace: Milla Jovovich's Open-Source AI Memory
item.description:
MemPalace is an open-source (MIT), local-first memory system for AI assistants, co-created by actress Milla Jovovich and developer Ben Sigman and released in April 2026. It stores your conversations and files verbatim, without summarizing them, sorts them into wings, rooms and drawers, and retrieves them with semantic search. Everything stays on your machine by default.

This page covers what MemPalace is, how its “palace” structure works, how to use it, and what its much-discussed benchmark numbers actually measure. Facts come from the MemPalace GitHub README and the official docs at mempalaceofficial.com, checked October 2026.

item.title: Cognee Alternatives: 7 Agent Memory Tools Compared
item.description: Cognee alternatives are other memory systems for AI agents: Mem0, Graphiti, Zep, Letta, Hindsight, MemPalace and Supermemory. People look for one when Cognee’s knowledge-graph pipeline is more than they need for simple per-user memory, when they want temporal fact tracking in open source, or when they want the agent itself to manage memory. For that second reason, Graphiti and Hindsight both fit; Graphiti needs a graph database, while Hindsight runs its graph and temporal recall on Postgres, all in the MIT release.

item.title: Letta Alternatives: 7 Agent Memory Options Compared
item.description:
Letta alternatives are memory systems you can use instead of Letta (formerly MemGPT) to give agents long-term memory. The main ones are Mem0, Zep, Graphiti, Cognee, LangMem, Hindsight and Supermemory. Most teams switch because they want a memory layer for their own agent, while Letta is now a full agent runtime that owns the loop.

This page covers what Letta does today, the common reasons to look elsewhere, a comparison table, a short section per option, and how to choose. For a deeper look at Letta itself, see the Letta guide.

item.title: Supermemory Alternatives: 7 Agent Memory Tools Compared
item.description:
Supermemory alternatives are other memory layers for AI agents: Hindsight, Mem0, Zep, Graphiti, Letta, Cognee and Honcho. People usually look for one when they need fully open-source, self-run infrastructure (Supermemory’s local server is a closed-source binary), want memory without bundled RAG and connectors, or need a different memory model such as a temporal graph or an agent that manages its own memory.

Below: what Supermemory does, a comparison table, a short section on each alternative, and how to pick. Facts come from each project’s README, docs and pricing page, checked on 8 October 2026.

item.title: Zep Alternatives: Open-Source and Hosted Options
item.description: Zep alternatives are other ways to give AI agents long-term memory: Graphiti (Zep’s own open-source core), Hindsight, Mem0, Letta, Cognee and Supermemory. Most people searching for one want a self-hosted, open-source option, because Zep stopped maintaining its Community Edition in 2025 and is now a managed, credit-priced service. Graphiti is the closest match to Zep’s model; Hindsight is the most complete open-source memory server, with graph and time-range recall, consolidation and reflect all in its MIT release.

item.title: Dify LLM Memory: Node Memory, Window Size, Variables
item.description:
Dify LLM memory is a per-node setting in Chatflow apps. Turn on Memory in an LLM node and Dify adds earlier turns of the same conversation to that node’s prompt. A window size caps how many turns load, and Dify trims further to fit the model’s context. For state you control, Chatflow also has conversation variables. Neither carries over to a new conversation.

This page covers how each mechanism behaves in Dify 1.17.1 (September 2026) and what 1.18.0 (October 2026) changed for agent sessions, drawn from the Dify docs and the open-source code, plus the options for long-term memory across conversations.

item.title: Zep Docker in 2026: Self-Hosting Options Explained
item.description:
You can’t self-host today’s Zep with Docker. Zep Community Edition, the Docker-based self-hosted Zep, has been deprecated since April 2025. What you can run in Docker now is Graphiti, Zep’s open-source temporal graph engine, as a REST server with Neo4j or an MCP server with FalkorDB. The full Zep product runs in your own cloud only on the Enterprise plan.

Many guides still show docker compose up for Zep. They describe an edition that gets no updates or support. This page lays out the real options, with working Compose setups, based on the getzep/zep and Graphiti repositories, checked on 6 November 2026 against Graphiti 0.31.2.

item.title: Zep vs Mem0: Temporal Graph vs Fact Memory
item.description: Zep vs Mem0 is a choice between two ways of storing what an agent learns. Zep keeps a temporal knowledge graph where every fact has a validity window, so old facts are invalidated rather than lost. Mem0 extracts short facts into a vector store with entity linking, and ranks them by semantic, keyword and entity match. Mem0 is open source; Zep is a managed service with Graphiti as its open-source core.

item.title: What Is Zep Memory? Zep Cloud, Graphiti and Pricing
item.description:
Zep memory is Zep Cloud, a managed service that stores what an agent learns from users and data in a temporal context graph, then returns a prompt-ready block of relevant facts. Its open-source core is Graphiti, a framework for knowledge graphs that track when facts change. The old self-hosted Zep Community Edition is deprecated.

This page covers what Zep is now, how Zep memory stores and retrieves data, the Zep paper, pricing, self-hosting, and integrations. Sources are Zep’s docs, the Graphiti repo and the Zep pricing page.

item.title: Why Is AI Memory So Bad? Why Chatbots Forget
item.description:
AI memory is so bad because the model behind a chatbot doesn’t remember anything by itself. It reads only the text placed in front of it for each reply. Long chats push old messages out, models handle long inputs unevenly, and memory features save just a selection of what you said. Each step drops information.

What is AI memory?

AI memory is everything a chatbot uses to recall information from outside the current reply: the recent conversation, saved facts, and searches over past chats. The language model doesn’t store your conversations in its weights. The app stores them and decides which pieces to feed back into the model’s input, called the context window.

item.title: Character.AI Memory Limit: Pins, Chat Memories, Lorebooks
item.description:
Character.AI’s memory limit is the amount of recent conversation a character can consider at once. Character.AI doesn’t publish that number. What it does publish: free users can pin 15 messages per chat and write 400 characters of fixed facts into Chat Memories. Anything outside those tools and the recent context can be forgotten.

What is Character.AI’s memory limit?

Character.AI’s memory limit is the cap on how much chat text a character reads before writing each reply. The company’s own FAQ puts it plainly: “There is a limited amount of conversation context that the character can consider, so it will appear to forget things if they were not mentioned recently” (Character.AI Help Center).

item.title: Vector Databases for LLM Memory: How to Choose One
item.description: A vector database for LLM memory stores past messages, facts and documents as embeddings, then finds the ones closest in meaning to the current query so they can be added to the prompt. It’s the storage layer under most long-term memory systems. For most teams the best choice is the database they already run (pgvector in Postgres, or Redis), with a dedicated vector database like Qdrant, Milvus or Pinecone once scale or multi-tenancy demands it.

item.title: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank: Guide and Pricing
item.description:
Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank is Google Cloud’s managed long-term memory for AI agents. It uses Gemini models to pull facts and preferences out of conversations, merges them with what it already knows about that user, and returns them later by scope or similarity search. In April 2026 Google renamed it Agent Platform Memory Bank, part of the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

Old links and code still use the Vertex name; the ADK class is still VertexAiMemoryBankService and takes an agent_engine_id. This page uses Google’s current docs, release notes and pricing page, checked on 8 October 2026.

item.title: What Is Mem0? How the Mem0 Memory Layer Works
item.description:
Mem0 (“mem-zero”) is an open-source memory layer for AI agents. It uses an LLM to pull durable facts out of conversations, stores them with embeddings per user, agent or session, and returns the relevant ones when you search. It ships as a Python and Node library, a self-hosted Docker server, and the managed Mem0 Platform.

This page explains how Mem0 works today, what changed in the April 2026 release, and how to configure, query and delete memories. Facts come from the Mem0 GitHub README, the Mem0 docs and the pricing page, checked on 8 October 2026; pricing rechecked on 30 October 2026 after Mem0’s 26 October change.

item.title: MemoryOS: The Memory OS of AI Agent Paper Explained
item.description:
MemoryOS is a memory system for AI agents that borrows ideas from how operating systems manage memory. It keeps conversation data in three tiers (short-term, mid-term and long-term persona memory) and moves it between them with fixed rules. The paper, “Memory OS of AI Agent,” appeared at EMNLP 2025 and reports a 49.11% average F1 gain on LoCoMo.

This page explains the MemoryOS paper and its GitHub repo, then places it next to the other “memory operating system” designs: MemGPT (now Letta) and MemOS. Facts come from the paper on arXiv, the ACL Anthology entry and the BAI-LAB/MemoryOS repo.

item.title: OpenAI Agents SDK Memory: Sessions and Sandbox Memory
item.description:
OpenAI Agents SDK memory comes in two parts. Sessions store a conversation’s history and replay it on every Runner.run, so the agent remembers earlier turns. Sandbox agent memory distills lessons from past runs into Markdown files the agent reads next time. There’s no built-in store of user facts across sessions.

This page covers both against the Python SDK (openai-agents 0.23, October 2026), using the official Sessions docs. It also clears up a common mix-up with ChatGPT’s own memory features.

item.title: ReasoningBank: Agent Memory That Learns From Failures
item.description:
ReasoningBank is a memory framework for LLM agents from Google that stores lessons, not logs. After each task, the agent judges whether it succeeded, then writes down a few general reasoning strategies, including warnings from its failures. On new tasks it retrieves the closest lessons. On WebArena with Gemini 2.5 Flash, it lifted success from 40.5% to 48.8%.

The paper is “ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory” by Siru Ouyang, Jun Yan, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister and 13 co-authors (arXiv 2509.25140), accepted at ICLR 2026. It also introduces MaTTS, a way to spend extra compute per task to produce better memories.

item.title: Short-Term vs Long-Term Memory in Agentic AI
item.description:
Short-term and long-term memory in agentic AI differ by scope. Short-term memory is the agent’s state for one task: messages, tool results, the plan. It lives in the prompt and ends with the thread. Long-term memory lives in an external store, survives across sessions, and is retrieved selectively. Agents need both, plus a path that moves information between them.

This page compares the two side by side and shows how they connect in code. Each type has its own deep dive: short-term memory in AI agents and AI agent long-term memory. The pillar, AI agent memory explained, covers the full taxonomy.

item.title: Hermes Agent Memory (2026): 2,200-Char Limit, 9 Providers, Fixes
item.description:
Hermes Agent memory is two small, agent-curated files plus a searchable history. MEMORY.md (2,200 characters) holds the agent’s own notes and USER.md (1,375 characters) holds your profile. Both load into the system prompt at session start. Older conversations live in SQLite and are searched on demand. One optional external provider can add more.

Hermes Agent is an open-source (MIT) agent from Nous Research that runs in a terminal, the Hermes Agent desktop app or messaging apps (all sharing the same memory) and creates reusable skills from its own experience. This page covers each layer of its memory, the external providers, and what to check when memory seems broken. Details come from the official Hermes memory docs, checked October 2026.

item.title: Hermes Agent 记忆：2,200 字符上限、记忆插件与故障排查
item.description:
Hermes Agent 的记忆由两个小文件加一份可搜索的历史组成。 这两个文件都由 agent 自己管理：MEMORY.md（2,200 字符）存 agent 的笔记，USER.md（1,375 字符）存你的资料。两者在会话开始时加载进系统提示词。较早的对话存在 SQLite 里，需要时再搜索。还可以再加一个外部插件。

Hermes Agent 是 Nous Research 开发的开源（MIT）agent。它可以在终端、Hermes Agent 桌面版 或聊天应用里运行（所有入口共享同一份记忆），还能从自己的经验中创建可复用的技能。本页介绍它记忆的每一层、外部插件，以及记忆看起来不工作时该检查什么。细节来自官方 Hermes 记忆文档，2026 年 10 月核对。

Hermes Agent 的记忆是什么？

Hermes Agent 的记忆是一个有容量上限、会跨会话保留的精选存储。 agent 决定保存什么，通过 memory 工具把简短条目写入 MEMORY.md 和 USER.md。每次会话开始时，Hermes 把两个文件作为冻结的一块注入系统提示词。

这个设计刻意保持小巧。两个文件合计约 1,300 个 token，始终在上下文里。其他内容（完整对话记录、旧任务）在 agent 搜索之前都不进入提示词。这种"始终加载的记忆 + 按需召回"的分工，与 AI agent 记忆解释 中描述的相同。第一次用 Hermes？Hermes Agent 指南 介绍了安装、设置，以及每个记忆文件放在哪里。

Hermes 记忆的各层

层 位置 大小 何时在上下文中
MEMORY.md ~/.hermes/memories/ 2,200 字符（约 800 个 token） 每次会话，作为冻结快照
USER.md ~/.hermes/memories/ 1,375 字符（约 500 个 token） 每次会话，作为冻结快照
会话历史 ~/.hermes/state.db（SQLite，FTS5） 无上限，除非开启自动清理 仅当 agent 调用 session_search 时
技能 技能目录 每个技能不同 技能相关时
外部插件 取决于插件 取决于插件 每轮对话前预取

使用 profile 时，文件位于 ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/memories/ 下。

item.title: Langflow Memory Chatbot: Message History and Sessions
item.description:
A memory chatbot in Langflow keeps earlier messages of a session and feeds them back to the model. The Agent component does this by default, loading up to 100 past messages for the same session_id. For plain model flows, the Message History component retrieves and stores chat history. Memory bases (added in Langflow 1.10) add semantic recall across sessions.

The details below follow the Langflow memory docs for the 1.13 release line (1.13.0, 22 October 2026), its release notes and the Langflow source code. If you’re upgrading, the 1.13 changes matter most for memory bases.

item.title: Mem0 Paper: Building Production-Ready AI Agents (2026)
item.description:
“Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory” is the 2025 paper from the Mem0 team that describes how Mem0 extracts, updates and retrieves memories from conversations. It introduces two systems, Mem0 and a graph-based variant called Mem0g, and reports that both beat other memory systems on the LoCoMo benchmark while using far fewer tokens than full-context prompting.

The paper is arXiv 2504.19413, by Prateek Chhikara, Dev Khant, Saket Aryan, Taranjeet Singh and Deshraj Yadav, submitted on 28 April 2025. Everything below comes from that paper unless another source is linked. All results in it are the authors’ own.

item.title: OpenClaw Memory: Files, Search and Embedding Models
item.description:
OpenClaw memory is a folder of Markdown files the agent writes and reads. MEMORY.md holds durable facts and decisions, USER.md holds your preferences, and dated daily notes hold running context. The first two load at session start. Everything is indexed in SQLite, and the agent finds older notes with memory_search, a hybrid of vector and keyword search.

OpenClaw is an open-source (MIT) personal AI assistant built by Peter Steinberger and contributors and now stewarded by the OpenClaw Foundation. It runs on your own machine and talks to you through WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, iMessage and 20+ other channels. Facts on this page come from the official memory docs and memory search docs, checked October 2026. New to OpenClaw? Start with the OpenClaw guide for install, onboarding and the Gateway.

item.title: OpenClaw vs Hermes Agent Memory: Side by Side
item.description:
OpenClaw vs Hermes Agent memory comes down to two philosophies. Hermes keeps memory tiny and fixed: two hard-capped files loaded as a frozen snapshot, plus full-text search over old sessions. OpenClaw keeps memory open-ended: Markdown files and daily notes, indexed for hybrid search, with a background job that promotes the best notes into MEMORY.md.

Both are open-source (MIT) agents that run on your machine and chat through messaging apps; Hermes also has an official desktop app that shares the CLI’s memory. OpenClaw comes from Peter Steinberger and the OpenClaw Foundation; Hermes Agent comes from Nous Research. Facts below come from each project’s docs, checked October 2026.

item.title: LLM Memory Survey Papers: The 6 Worth Reading (2026)
item.description:
An LLM memory survey is a review paper that sorts the research on how language models and agents store, update and recall information. Six surveys on arXiv cover most of the field as of October 2026. Start with Zhang et al. (2024) for the basics, then read Hu et al.’s “Memory in the Age of AI Agents” (December 2025) for the current map.

Each one splits memory differently. That’s the useful part: the taxonomies show which questions the field treats as open. This page summarizes each survey from its arXiv paper, with links to the abstract and the full text.

item.title: LLM Parametric Memory: What Model Weights Remember
item.description:
LLM parametric memory is the knowledge a language model stores in its weights during training. It’s why a model knows Paris is in France without being told. It’s free to use at query time, but it’s frozen after training, can’t be updated per user, and is hard to inspect or correct. That’s why agents put user and task memory somewhere else.

This page covers how facts end up in weights, how much a model can hold, how to change it, and the “latent memory” research that sits between weights and text. For how parametric memory fits next to the memory types agents actually manage, see AI agent memory explained.

item.title: Hierarchical Memory for LLM Agents: Tiers and Trees
item.description:
Hierarchical memory for LLMs organizes what an agent remembers into levels instead of one flat list. There are two main kinds. Tiered hierarchies split memory by speed and size, like a computer’s RAM and disk. Abstraction hierarchies stack summaries on top of raw records, so the agent can answer broad questions without reading everything. Most current agent memory systems use one or both.

This page explains both kinds, the systems that defined them, and when a hierarchy beats a flat vector store.

item.title: LLM Memory Comparison: 11 Memory Systems Side by Side
item.description:
This LLM memory comparison puts eleven memory systems for LLM agents side by side: what license they use, how they store memories, how they retrieve them, whether you can self-host, and which benchmarks they publish. Every fact was checked against the project’s GitHub README or docs on 8 October 2026. Where a number is self-reported, the table says so.

This page is the fact sheet. For advice on which one to pick, see how to choose the best AI memory framework. For the concepts behind the columns, see AI agent memory explained.

item.title: LLM Memory Compression: Compaction, Summaries, Tokens
item.description:
LLM memory compression means fitting what a model needs to remember into fewer tokens or fewer bytes. In practice it’s five different techniques: summarizing old conversation turns (compaction), extracting facts instead of keeping transcripts, pruning tokens from prompts, evicting entries from the model’s KV cache, and quantizing stored embeddings. Each one trades some detail for cost, speed or room in the context window.

This page explains each technique, what the papers and API docs report, and when to use which.

item.title: LLM Memory Evaluation: Benchmarks for Agent Memory
item.description:
LLM memory evaluation means testing whether a model or agent can recall, update and reason over information from earlier sessions. The standard benchmarks are LoCoMo and LongMemEval, with MemoryAgentBench and BEAM as harder, newer tests. Each feeds a long chat history to the system, then asks questions only that history can answer.

The tests differ in what they stress: plain recall, time, changed facts, forgetting, or scale. Picking the wrong one tells you little about your use case. Two 2026 benchmarks, FEB-30 and Bemula, go further and score the memory store itself rather than the answer, and three late-October papers split recall from the decision made with it. This page covers what each benchmark measures, how it’s scored, and how to run one yourself.

item.title: Janitor AI Memory (2026): JLLM's 9K Context, Chat Memory and Fixes
item.description:
Janitor LLM memory is how much of a roleplay chat the bot can see at once. On Janitor AI’s free model, JanitorLLM (JLLM), that’s a context window of roughly 8,000 to 9,000 tokens, shared between the bot’s permanent definition, your Chat Memory note and the most recent messages. Anything older silently drops out, which is why bots forget.

The fix isn’t a hidden setting. It’s managing that token budget: keep definitions lean, keep a short Chat Memory note, and refresh it with summaries. This page explains how each part works, using Janitor’s help center and changelog, checked on 1 November 2026.

item.title: Largest Context Window Open-Source LLMs (Local, 2026)
item.description: The largest context window open-source LLM as of November 2026 is Llama 4 Scout, with 10M tokens. A wider group supports about 1M: Llama 4 Maverick, Kimi K3 and the new Kimi K3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4, GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M3, Mistral Large 4 and Meta’s Muse Spark Open.
